PluginManifest.Name: Kurisu.VoiceOverTools
PluginManifest.Title: Dialogue System Voice Over Helper
PluginManifest.Description: Voice-over asset helpers for dialogue projects. Rename VO files to a consistent {hexId}_{culture} scheme, clean up orphaned audio assets not referenced by any DialogueFragment, and strip non-primary translations + voice-over references in one pass. All commands include a dry-run preview.
PluginManifest.Tags: Voice-Over, Dialogue, Asset Management, Rename, Localization
PluginManifest.ReleaseNotes: V1.0.0- Initial release version V1.0.1- Purge Voice Over and Translations Feature V1.0.2- Added "Clean Up Orphaned Voice-Overs" command with dry-run / delete-Articy / delete-Articy+disk options. Added dry-run preview window to Rename commands with per-entry status (already correct / will rename / display-only / target exists / source missing) and click-to-navigate. New Articy-style dark theme for all plugin windows. Bug fixes: RemoveVoiceOvers now resumes localization state handling on exception; silent-placeholder WAV is cleaned from disk after removal; removed dead helpers and unused imports. V1.0.3- Plugin renamed from Kurisu.VoiceOverNamingScheme to Kurisu.VoiceOverTools (manifest Name, C# namespace, assembly, filenames). NOTE: this is a breaking rename — Articy treats it as a new plugin; uninstall the old one via Package Manager before installing 1.0.3. No behavioral changes. V1.0.4- Added "Audit Voice-Overs" command (Global): scans every DialogueFragment and flags VO references that are missing for a language, corrupted (broken proxy / file missing on disk / 0-byte file), or overlapping (the same audio asset is shared by multiple distinct fragments). Read-only diagnostic with per-category filter toggles and click-to-navigate (Show Fragment / Show VO Asset). V1.0.5- Audit Voice-Overs filtering: hard-filter excludes fragments with no Speaker assigned (narration / stage directions don't get false-positive "Missing VO" entries). New per-character dropdown filter combines with the category toggles. Each row's header now includes the speaker name for at-a-glance scanning. V1.0.6- Audit row redesign for transparency. Each entry now shows the navigator path of the fragment, the actual dialogue line in the audited language, and the issue detail in a structured 4-line layout with proper visual hierarchy (category icon + label, speaker, id+lang, path, quoted line, detail). Full ComboBox / ComboBoxItem template overrides so the character-filter dropdown is properly themed (was unreadable in dark mode previously). V1.0.7- Audit property + empty-line filtering. Each row now shows which text property the issue is for (.Text, .PreviewText, etc.) as a small monospaced badge in the header. New per-property toggle row dynamically built from the property names found in the audit (hidden when only one property type is present). New "Include empty lines" checkbox — hides rows whose dialogue text is blank by default (fragments not yet written), opt-in to include them. V1.0.8- Audit by-path filter + UX polish. New "Path:" dropdown listing all path prefixes found in the audit (top-level folders, sub-folders, deeper) — picking a prefix narrows results to fragments under that branch. Works at any depth. All filters (categories / property / character / path / include-empty) consolidated into the summary panel for a cleaner hierarchy. Custom-templated CheckBox so the empty-lines toggle blends with the dark theme (was previously default-WPF-styled and out of place). Third grid row simplified to nav-buttons-only. V1.0.9- Audit UX iteration. Empty-lines toggle promoted from a separate checkbox to a 4th category-style pill (off by default) so all primary filters share the same visual language. Character + Path filters moved back to the toolbar row alongside the Show buttons. Path picker rebuilt as a hierarchical ContextMenu — top-level folders cascade rightward into subfolders to any depth, with a "(this folder)" entry under each parent so you can filter at any intermediate level. Themed MenuItem / Separator / ContextMenu so the dropdown matches the dark palette. V1.0.10- Audit dropdown stripe fix. ContextMenu is a logical-tree island in WPF — implicit MenuItem styles defined at the Window level were not propagating into it, so menu items rendered with the default Aero template (white-on-light icon column gutter on the left). Fixed by merging the theme dictionaries into the ContextMenu's own Resources and assigning the themed style explicitly to every MenuItem and Separator built in code. V1.0.11- Stripe fix v2 + Kurisu submenu. v1.0.10 didn't fully eliminate the white stripe in the path picker. v1.0.11 extracts the ControlTemplates as keyed resources and assigns them DIRECTLY on the ContextMenu and every MenuItem in code (Style propagation through Popup boundaries is unreliable in WPF). Also overrides Aero's role-keyed SubmenuItem/SubmenuHeader templates so the default never gets a chance to apply. V1.0.12- Kurisu submenu (correct separator). Articy uses BACKSLASH not slash as the submenu separator in CaptionLid (per https://www.articy.com/adxdevkit/html/writing_a_plugin.htm). v1.0.11 used 'Kurisu/' which Articy rendered as a literal flat command name. Switched to 'Kurisu\\' so all five commands now actually group under a Kurisu submenu in the ribbon and right-click menu. V1.1.7- Fix: Import silently did nothing when a voice-over was replaced again with a file of the same name, because articy skips a replacement whose file name and date match the last file it imported for that asset (proven by the self-test 2026-11-27: the same file landed once its date alone was changed). Every staged file now gets the current date. articy also finishes the copy in the background up to about a second after it reports being done, so each replacement now waits for the stored file to hold the new audio (up to 10 s) before it counts, and staged copies are kept until all rows are checked. The self-test swaps and restores through the real import; its by-hand diagnostics run only if the import fails. V1.1.6- Fix: Import could report a voice-over as replaced while articy kept the old file (ChangeAsset returned without error and changed nothing); every replacement is now checked against the stored file and marked Failed if it did not take. Self-test: the swap goes through the real import path and, if articy skips the file, offers the same file again with only its date refreshed, to show whether articy skips a file whose name and date match its last import. The report names the plugin code that actually ran next to the installed version, since articy keeps running an already-loaded plugin after an update until it restarts. V1.1.5- Self-test fixes. The 1.1.4 guard against an undone swap refused every voice-over in a project that stores a language as a copy of another (one test project: 278 lines, each recording stored as both el and en); it now only refuses audio shared with a different line. A project with no voice-overs now reports SKIP instead of a failure. V1.1.4- Self-test diagnostics. In 1.1.3 the self-test's restore step did not land (the swapped-in audio stayed; found and undone by hand 2026-11-25). The restore is now instrumented: it reports whether the plan saw a clean replace, whether ChangeAsset threw, and whether the stored file changed immediately, after the processing wait or within 10 s; if not, it retries once with the staged file's date set to now, and states which explanation fits. The self-test also refuses to swap a voice-over whose audio is identical to another one's (a sign an earlier swap was never undone), and warns that a replacement is written to disk at once. V1.1.3- Match Language Voice-Overs preview shows why each pair matched, so it can be checked by eye: the shared name it matched on, then the existing voice-over and the new one, each with its real file name (what is matched) and its articy name (shown only, never matched on), the new asset's folder, and whether it won by being named for the language or by having no suffix. Dropdowns and unmatched rows use the same file-name-first labels. V1.1.2- New "Match Language Voice-Overs..." (ribbon and right-click). Binds audio assets already imported into articy (one asset folder, subfolders optional) as the voice-overs of a target language, by matching their names to the voice-overs each slot already has in other languages: the tag and a trailing _language for any project language are ignored, so name_el, name_en and name all match, and _de counts for de-DE. Among assets sharing a name, one named for the target language wins, then one without a language; one named for another language is never used. Two equally good assets, or a slot that already has a different target voice-over, are conflicts that stay as they are until you pick. Every binding is read back after it is set. Covered by 446 new articy-free checks, including a synthetic project of 400 slots, and proven against three deliberately broken versions of the rules. V1.1.1- Export / Import hardening from an articy-free test suite (Tests/, 879 checks, including a synthetic round trip of 302 bindings through all 96 option combinations). Fixed: a folder named after a Windows device with a dot, such as "aux.wav", could not be created (now "aux_.wav"). A tag is now 4 or more hex digits right after the name, so "line (2)" is never read as one. Import: identical copies of one file (a shared voice-over exported into several branches) count as one; a file whose tag differs from the stored one, and an empty file, are conflicts; a conflict is applied only when a file is picked in its dropdown. Export: paths over Windows' 260-character limit are refused in the preview instead of failing on write. New "Self-Test Export / Import (copies only)" command: exports and re-plans everything under the picked object, swaps one voice-over for another file and restores it, and reports what articy did. V1.1.0- "Export / Import Voice-Overs..." (ribbon and right-click). One window, two modes, sharing the picked object (articy's own picker; the right-clicked object is pre-picked), a folder, languages and a main language. Export copies every voice-over under the object: the main language loses its _language suffix, the (XXXX) tag can be kept or stripped, files can be split into one top folder per language, 0-6 hierarchy levels and a speaker folder before or after the hierarchy, and existing files are skipped or overwritten. Import searches a folder and its subfolders and replaces voice-overs whose stored names match (exactly when the file keeps its tag, ignoring the tag when it does not, and with the main-language suffix optional); a file matching several voice-overs, several files matching one, or a different file format are listed as conflicts and never resolved for you. Files identical to the stored ones are skipped. Replaced assets keep their display name, description and external id. Both modes preview first. Built against Articy.MDK 2.4.1 (articy 4.4). V1.0.17- Menu and icon. Commands now sit under "Firecrest Roost: Voice-Over Tools" instead of "Kurisu". Articy never merges submenus across plugins, so with a second Kurisu plugin installed the shared "Kurisu" root appeared twice. The plugin uses the Firecrest Roost bird as its icon. V1.0.16- Multi-bound warning in the rename planner. New 6th category-style toggle "Multi-bound" (visible by default) — counts and optionally hides plan entries whose VO asset is bound to >1 distinct DialogueFragment project-wide (not limited to the rename scope, since the underlying file is shared across all bound fragments). Multi-bound rows render with a tinted background regardless of toggle state. Pre-execute confirmation dialog: when the actionable plan (Will rename + Display only) contains any multi-bound entries, a warning dialog explains the failure mode (each bound fragment overwrites the asset's filename + display + ExternalId, so only the last-processed fragment ends up with correct metadata) and offers Cancel / Proceed. No change to rename behavior — this is informative + a confirmation gate, not a code-path branch. V1.0.15- Fix: rename pass's "Rename Complete" report flashed open then immediately closed, leaving Articy in a stuck-modal state where the main UI was unresponsive as if a dialog were still open. Root cause: Session.ChangeAsset internally pops its own ProgressDialogWrapper for each reimported asset; Session.WaitForAssetProcessing waits for assets to be clean but not for the progress dialogs' close events to drain off the UI dispatcher. When the report opened against that pending state, MessageBoxEx.GetTargetWindow returned the dying progress dialog as the owner, and the report closed with it. Fix: drain the dispatcher to ApplicationIdle priority inside ShowReport before showing, so progress-dialog cleanup completes and Keyboard.FocusedElement settles on the main Articy window first. Drain is shared so the cleanup-orphaned report path also gets the protection. V1.0.14- Filter MarkupText alongside BBCodeText in the new tools' text-property iteration. Both are calculated CustomProperty views over the same underlying .Text (BBCodeText = BBCode rendering, MarkupText = XAML rich-text rendering used by the in-app rich-text editor) — they're not independent text fields. Including MarkupText produced phantom duplicate-translation groups that mirrored the .Text groups exactly. Now matched against Articy's own internal exclusion pattern for these two property names. V1.0.13- Two new tools. "Find Duplicate Translations" scans every DialogueFragment's localized text properties and groups together fragments whose non-reference-language text is byte-identical — useful for spotting copy-pasted translations that should have differed. Picker for reference language (defaults to project primary), comparison toggles (case-insensitive, collapse whitespace, include groups where every member shares the same reference text), and view filters (offending language, character, navigator path). Per-row Clear / Clear from others; footer Clear-all-filtered with per-language confirmation breakdown. "Find Multi-bound Voice-Overs" inverts the audit's Overlapping view into a per-asset listing — one entry per audio asset bound to more than one DialogueFragment, with a sub-row for each binding. Group header has Play (system audio decoder), Show VO Asset, and asset metadata; sub-rows have Clear / Clear from others. Optional toggle to also flag intra-fragment overlaps. Clears use the API-supported null assignment for VoiceOverReferences (verified against the live LocalizationHelper.SetAudioSample chain).
